question.text: Units of a close-ended AIF may be listed on a stock exchange with a minimum tradable lot of:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI AIF Regulations, units of a close-ended AIF may be listed on a stock exchange, subject to a minimum tradable lot of INR 1 crore. Listing is permitted only after the final close of the fund or respective scheme; it is not mandatory. The Trap: The lower-rupee options (INR 10 lakh, INR 50 lakh) are designed to invite confusion with general retail lot sizes, but the AIF tradable lot is kept at INR 1 crore to preserve the sophisticated-investor threshold; INR 5 crore overshoots the prescribed lot. Note: Listing of AIF units is permitted but not mandatory, and it can happen only after the final close of the fund or scheme. The INR 1 crore minimum tradable lot preserves the sophisticated-investor threshold even on the secondary market.
